upstream_sources.role: Compared the later Plus and SE patch dispatcher. Its expanded table and register allocation differ from the target ROM.

boundary_evidence.start: Dispatch begins at $401F4A immediately after PinRect. EMT1010 begins at $401F52 and shares the dispatcher body.
boundary_evidence.end: GetTrapAddress ends with RTS at $40202E. Memory Manager queue routines begin at $402030.

edits.description: Restored both exception-frame entries, Toolbox auto-pop handling, OS register preservation, and GetTrapAddress and SetTrapAddress from the ROM. The released Dispatch.a history records a rewrite in November 1988 and removal of 68000 paths in May 1992. Its retained interface description defines the old behavior.

Restored the Plus table addresses, $0400 for OS traps and $0C00 for Toolbox traps, with a 9-bit Toolbox mask. The selector bits agree with the released old/new trap numbering description. Bit 8 controls A0 preservation; bit 10 selects Toolbox auto-pop.

Retained the original header, early history, applicable calling convention description, and trap-address routine contracts. Omitted later processor timing, cache flushing, patch protection, and extended Toolbox paths.

Assembled every instruction from a mnemonic and operands. The module contains no data directives or instruction placeholders. ROM branch destinations and widths are explicit. Descriptive local labels do not claim to reproduce lost original names.

verification.method: Called the shared verify_module function in an independent temporary directory. It assembled MC68000 code, linked at the ROM address, checked all entry points and relocations, and compared every emitted byte.
verification.scope: The entire emitted span matches the ROM. MPW assembly has not been run. The released source no longer contains the original bodies; these are ROM restorations supported by the retained interface description.
